rules.rule: makeRng is a Park-Miller recurrence: multiplier 16807, modulus 2147483647, unsigned seed conversion and zero fallback 1.
With seed 1 the recurrence's first integer is 16807.
An effect owns one generator shared across emitters; HunFXEffect.play resets that stream and EmitterSim.play does not independently reseed it.

Spawn consumes shape draws, curve draws and per-particle stored random values; particle state later reuses those stored fractions; burst/rate evaluations also consume draws, so emitter traversal order and enabled branches participate in the sequence.
The pixel sampler uses Math.random() after its initial 40000 samples; UI dice and unspecified effect seeds also use unseeded randomness.
Scalar curves support constant c, random interval r, scaled Hermite k and blended scaled Hermite rk; missing or unknown scalar curves return 0.
Hermite clamps endpoints and uses the left key's index 3 tangent and the right key's index 2 tangent with segment duration.

Color evaluation supports constant/ranged colors and single/ranged gradients; color and alpha keys are independent; fixed mode chooses interpolation fraction 1 for an interior segment; missing color input gives white.
Color conversion uses the piecewise gamma-to-linear rule at 0.04045 and 1, with exponent 2.2 above 1.
rules.note: Breakpoints and the exponent are stated; the full expression for the interior branch is not enumerated by the report.

rules.rule: Capacity is min(def.max || 1000, 256).
Configured maxima 3, 256 and 300 produce capacities 3, 256 and 256; an absent maximum produces 256.
Play clears particles and delay/rate/burst/cycle/stopped state.

Loop+prewarm repeatedly updates at 1/60 while accumulated time is below duration, then sets preT to duration and shifts delay; it does not use an integer fixed-step count and the report does not claim exact elapsed integration.
Life minimum is 0.01.
Shape types are sphere/hemisphere 0-3, cones 4/7/8/9, circles 10/11 and box 5; shape position is scaled, rotated Z-X-Y and translated.
Unsupported shape codes keep the initial origin/+Z before transforms.
The emission clock applies a delay gate, a duration-inclusive one-shot gate, modulo loop time, per-cycle burst reset, repeat catch-up and a fractional rate accumulator.

Spawn attributes are normalized system time, life minimum 0.01, scalar/3D size and rotation, direction alignment, initial color/flip/randoms; world-space position and velocity are transformed at emission.
Age advances before the death check; particles reaching life are removed before motion.
Gravity is applied then force-over-life; magnitude damping then exponential drag.
Motion multiplies base+velocity-over-life by the speed modifier, then applies orbital rotations/radial motion, then sequential sinusoidal noise.
Total velocity is derived from the final displacement over dt when dt exceeds 1e-6, rather than only base velocity.
Trail history applies spawn probability, local/world conversion, minimum-distance insertion and strict age-greater-than lifetime pruning.
Render state covers size/rotation/color-over-life, RGB linearization, lifetime/FPS sheet addressing, row selection, negative wrapping and custom channels.
Effect update caps incoming dt at 0.25 before tempo.
_advance steps only while t + 1/120 <= clock + 1e-9; it does not advance until t exceeds clock.
Backward seek restarts using the stored seed.
Completion requires every emitter to have no live particles and no remaining emission; stop suppresses new emission but allows existing particles to finish.

Existing world particles are converted back through the emitter inverse for GPU output; holder transforms and attribute writes implement the Unity/three handedness boundary; world matrices are refreshed for world particles/trails.
Render modes are billboard 0, stretched 1 and mesh/oriented-quad 4; geometry comes from the mesh asset or the shared quad.

Mesh pivot uses geometry bounds; the holder transform flips z and quaternion x/y signs; render order incorporates emitter index and fudge; per-frame writes optionally depth-sort and set instance count/dirty flags.
Trail geometry uses at most 1024 stretched segment instances with midpoint/direction/width/arc-length UVs and a separate material, drawn before its particle mesh.
Material dispatch distinguishes simple, stencil, builtin-additive and common/legacy shaders.
Keywords control gas alpha, color, dissolve color, position scroll, fresnel, depth fade and vertex offset.
Missing texture references use white.
Blending is additive One/One or straight-alpha SrcAlpha/OneMinusSrcAlpha, with depth writing off.
Depth fading uses an analytic floor approximation, not a sampled scene-depth texture.
Texture wrapping follows clamp; texture colorSpace is NoColorSpace because the shader receives explicit sRGB flags.
Capture quantizes requested advancement by round(seconds*60) updates of 1/60, each reaching the effect's 1/120 clock.
The bounds pass uses 256-square black/white captures and an alpha threshold of 30.
Bounds are unioned across frames and a 1:1/2:1/1:2 shape is chosen using ratio 1.7.
Final capture uses an integer supersampling factor clamped 2-8, restarts the effect, then renders black, white and half-intensity black per output frame.

Alpha is the clamped maximum of channelwise 255-minus-background-difference; RGB is unpremultiplied from the half-intensity image; rows are flipped; the stored representation keeps half-color headroom.
The library shader clock advances in HunFX.update; capture restarts effects but does not reset that library clock between passes.
Capture loop determination uses absent/nonpositive duration.
The application limits demo environment width to 160.
Capture options apply slash category orientation, side-view roll, catalog-based search size, duration/loop/fps/warmup, layer hiding and demo size restrictions.
pixelate rejects empty captures and invalid dimensions.
Output dimensions come from shape or explicit outW/outH; source blocks are alpha-weighted; the half-color factor 2 is restored; white-hot brightening is applied.
Optional gradient mapping samples luminance, uses 2nd/98th percentiles with a minimum span, adjusts faint-alpha placement and mixes a LUT.
Hue/saturation and edge darkening precede alpha quantization.
Alpha at or below threshold becomes 0; one alpha level makes survivors opaque; otherwise ceiling quantization produces steps.
Auto-bright derives gain from 90th-percentile luminance unless gradient mapping is enabled.
Custom palettes bypass median cut; otherwise median-cut sampling generates a shared sequence palette.
Cleanup removes small 8-connected foreground components and optionally fills enclosed 4-connected holes.
Bayer 2/4 dithering precedes nearest-color selection.
Inner/outer outlines use 4 or 8 neighbors and can add an outline color not included in the returned palette list.
Palette imports accept text hex colors or distinct opaque image colors.
The gradient editor supports 2-8 stops, sorted positions and conversion of the legacy reverse flag.
Holds are integer 0-8, where 0 drops a frame.
Markers express time independently of fps.
applyHolds removes dropped frames, bakeHolds duplicates survivors, totalTime sums holds/fps and stepped holds group frames.
Holds [1,0,3] give two retained frames and four baked frames.
rules.derivation: frame1 hold 1 retained -> 1 baked; frame2 hold 0 dropped; frame3 hold 3 retained -> 3 baked; retained = 2, baked = 1 + 3 = 4

rules.rule: Saved timing is keyed by frame-count and fps; recommendation marks are not automatically applied to default playback, whose holds default to 1; the UI prevents all-zero holds.
Preview advances displayed frames according to those holds.
Ambient presets and parameter specifications are code-defined; a seeded builder constructs layers and drawEnvFrame evaluates their paths as a function of loop phase.
Supported ambient drawing includes falling/rising/drifting/twinkling particles, bolts, splash and fog; optional sprite images can be used.
envCapture evaluates frames into a supersampled Canvas and returns the common capture representation.
Sprite capture loads/caches sheet images, selects cells, supports recolor ramps, range/fps/speed and geometric flip/rotation, then returns frames for the same pixel stage.

Ambient RNG is separate from particle RNG: rngFrom uses a different integer generator and combines the user seed with a hash of preset ID; counts scale with canvas area (fog with its square root); depth tiers vary size/alpha; capture stores half-color and returns explicit dimensions and loop=true.
Sheet/PNG: layout picks a grid or fixed columns, draws ImageData frames into a sheet and PNG uses Canvas blob encoding.
GIF: global indexed palette, optional transparency/background compositing, alpha cutoff 128, integer scaling, own LZW, max 256 colors and cumulative centisecond delay rounding.
encodeGif has a loop option, but the application call omits loop:o.loop; its default writes the repeat extension's infinite value.
ZIP uses store-mode entries with CRC32 and directory records.
Aseprite: RGBA document, layer/cel chunks, zlib compression and hold-based frame durations.
JSON: frame rectangles/durations plus dimensions, fps, loop, origin and caller metadata.
Godot: AtlasTexture regions and SpriteFrames animation with hold-derived durations.
Unity: TextureImporter sprite-sheet metadata with ppu/pivot and per-sprite rectangles.
Unity metadata generates identifiers with crypto.getRandomValues; repeated metadata generation is not specified as byte-identical by a particle seed.
Export ranges are 1-based inclusive in the UI and become zero-based slices; range selection precedes hold removal/baking.
File paths group by format, optionally effect/view; JSON/Godot/Unity each receive their own sheet copy.
Batch jobs expand effects by views and seed variations, but sprites use one view/variation; each job is handled independently and errors are logged rather than terminating the whole loop.
Demo exports are restricted twice: the settings/UI clamp and the filesFor format selection allow sheet/frames/GIF only.

Desktop output calls preload IPC and writes files directly; browser output uses a directory handle when available or accumulates a ZIP download; Electron write paths are resolved under the chosen root and can fall back to Documents for specified permission errors at the default destination.
Settings bindings classify changes as recapture (cap), pixel-only reprocess (px) or export-only; recapture is debounced 350ms and gradient pixel changes 60ms.
The capture cache keys effect ID plus serialized capture options, retains up to 12 entries and is memory-only.
open guards asynchronous results with a token; locked effects clear preview; errors surface file/line-derived context; this is stale-result suppression, not a general cancellation mechanism.

Persistent JSON state includes settings, selected IDs, presets, current effect, language, creator flag and creator recommendations; settings include seeds, timing, hidden layers, environment overrides, sprite tints and output directory; presets deliberately omit per-effect fields and preserve them on application.
UI-size preference is separately stored as hun0fx.pixel.ui; DPR-aware sizing rounds to integral physical pixels.
Language selection normalizes locale codes and falls back to English or key text; DOM translation supports text/title/placeholder attributes.

The HTTP server binds 127.0.0.1, prefers port 47621 for a full-pack installation or 47622 otherwise, falls back to an ephemeral port on server error, requires a random URL prefix and performs a normalized-path prefix check.
Main-process full-edition detection is file existence of data/hun0fx.pak; renderer demo detection is manifest.edition === 'demo'; they are separate decisions.

window.__studio exposes orchestration functions and installs the bridge; bridge methods list/filter effects, read/update settings, preview, modify timing/seed/palette/gradient/env/sprite, manage presets and plan/encode exports.

The full-only control server requires POST plus a random key, limits request body size, invokes the renderer bridge and records connection metadata in userData; the preload always exists and mcp-config returns empty for demo.

External links are opened through the Electron shell rather than a new in-app window; old runtime directory cleanup is delayed 20 seconds and guarded by launcher environment and parent directory name runtime; window close removes MCP metadata and quits.
The manifest identifies hun0fx-pixel-studio-demo, product hun0fx Pixel Studio Demo, version 1.2.0 and main entry electron/main.js; the renderer separately declares display version 1.2.

HunFXPost defines half-float HDR targets, multilevel bright-pass/downsample/separable blur, bloom composition, Neutral-style tonemapping and vignette, but it is not invoked by the inspected studio Capture path, which imports HunFX and calls renderer.render directly.

HunFX caches definitions, pending loads, textures and meshes; definition loading supports variant patches and mixes that copy selected emitter layers, shift delays, transform scale/position and merge required assets.

create requires a loaded definition; play places an effect, adds lift, applies tuning and seed, attaches it to the chosen parent and tracks it; library updates advance shared shader time and dispose completed live effects when configured.
Placement helpers derive category presets and actor axes, support direction/quaternion/position and distinguish attachment from world placement.
Mesh buffers use supplied positions/UVs/indices/normals, computing normals if absent; the loader does not itself apply a blanket z inversion to mesh positions.

mountPak reads H0PK magic and index length, decodes the index, maps paths to offset/length/flags, caches reads, intercepts fetch only for known data-root paths and supplies texture blob URLs through three's loading manager; compressed entries use deflate and the texture URL path only handles uncompressed entries synchronously.
rules.note: The H0PK wire schema itself is not in the report; this rule describes the reader's behaviour only.
